The extension preserves the node's own message without relabelling the arm as a physical sensor.

No catalogue class binds one gym-style environment step that publishes a normalized nine-element incremental joint action, requests one Webots time_step and returns the joint positions read after it. cap.world.step.v1 takes ticks and requires a tick and state_hash; cap.motion.joint_position.v1 takes absolute positions and requires a reached result. The extension preserves the node's publication, its step service and its sensor sample; the publication itself stays unacknowledged.
catalogue_requests.summary: Publish one nine-joint action, call /webots/step once and read /joint_sensors/value after it.

catalogue_requests.reason: cap.world.step.v1 takes ticks and returns an observation, tick and state_hash. The node's /webots/step callback requests one Webots robot/time_step (the request value is fixed to 80 ms) and returns only a transport success; it returns no observation, reward, tick, termination or state hash. The extension preserves the one-request step.
catalogue_requests.summary: Request one Webots robot/time_step advance through /webots/step.

catalogue_requests.reason: cap.world.reset.v1 takes a scenario, options and seed and requires an observation and seed in its result. The node's /webots/reset callback takes no request fields, calls the Webots supervisor simulation_reset, requests one 8 ms step and returns a boolean; it has no seed or observation output. The extension preserves the native reset and is the declared safe-state action.

No catalogue class binds the gym environment's scalar reward service. cap.sensing.read.v1 binds physical sensor resources and selects named fields; the node's /reward callback returns a derived negative joint-distance sum for the environment, not a physical sensor channel.
catalogue_requests.summary: Read the environment reward scalar from /reward.

HISTORICAL (superseded by the 2026-11-05 repair paragraph at the end where they conflict): BLOCKED (HELPER_MISSING): the RosDriver can bind the pinned ROS 1 surface, but the stock helper cannot give the node's primary actuation the input-dependent observable effect that conformance TCAP-003 requires. Last gate run (2026-11-05T09:24:04Z, backend fake): G1 pass, G2 pass, G3 pass, G4 pass, G5 pass, G6 pass, G7 pass, G8 fail with G8.CONFORMANCE (MHS-Sim CL1; failing required test TCAP-003) and G8.TEST, G9 skip. Report digest sha256:4d5c5a2d957293801a146cb3f4e87c0f8e847d7aa1fb25579bfd1f0813d57626.

The blocker: the only input-bearing capability is the /joint_actuators/value gym_env/ActuatorMessage publication (src/gym_env_webots_node.cpp:258). Its callback adds motorRange[i]*actions[i]/20 to a static setpoint, clamps the result and calls the per-joint set_position services (117-125); it publishes nothing back. The effect is visible only after a separate /webots/step call (144-164, 253), and a RosDriver command binds exactly one service, action or topic. The publication receipt is {published: true, confirmed: false} for every input, so TCAP-003 sees identical outputs and an unchanged resource state. The only ways to pass would be a fake-only output or resource state that the real interface does not have, or pretending the action service applies the vector; the package does neither. The fake only records the publication and does not simulate joint motion.

Safety: the node advertises /joint_sensors, /joint_actuators, /webots/step, /webots/close, /webots/reset and /reward (250-256); none is a stop or pause. /webots/close only logs Close and returns true (166-169). The reset is declared as the input-free safe-state action: it asks the Webots supervisor to reset the simulation, requests one 8 ms time_step, loops until it succeeds and re-enables the sensors (171-195), restoring the initial simulated world. It does not stop the Webots process, cancel a queued step or fence other /joint_actuators/value publishers, and no independent hardware stop exists or is claimed. The runtime latches in software and the safe-state action is achieved by the reset; the reference correctly reports no native stop (software latch only). The action capability is R2 (robot arm; card floor R0) per MHS/spec/04-safety.md. The fake answers the safe-state reset immediately; that proves the declared ROS call and output contract, not that a Webots process or unrelated ROS clients stopped.

Implemented and checked: the /joint_sensors/value gym_env/SensorMessage subscription (source_ref 259, type include 16), the /joint_actuators/value gym_env/ActuatorMessage publication (258, include 17), /webots/step gym_env/StepEnv (253, include 20), /webots/reset gym_env/ResetEnv (255, include 19) and /reward gym_env/GetReward (256, include 21) as extension capabilities. The nine-element action length comes from MOTOR_NUMBER (25) and the motor_names order (44-46); the normalized -1.0..1.0 action bound is the actuatorSpacesCallback space (108-113; the callback scales by range/20 and clamps the joint setpoint at 117-125). The gym_env message/service definitions are external: the clone only declares the gym_env dependency (package.xml:52-63) and includes its headers (9-21). The StepEnv and ResetEnv response fields are not defined in the clone; the declared empty-response application predicate ($ == {}) is the expected empty-values contract, not a field read from a definition.
